text:
Ben P: FYI — Vendor 'CloudMetrics LLC' (TX) says they uploaded a resale certificate but our invoices still show TX sales tax (8.25%) on monthly hosted API charges. Invoice INV-2026-01 and INV-2026-02 attached. Can finance confirm whether we should reverse tax or request a signed form?
Aisha (Finance): Did we get a signed Texas Form 01-339 (Resale Certificate)? Texas requires the seller to keep the certificate on file. If it's a valid blanket resale certificate naming Redwood Inference, we can apply the exemption prospectively but need the effective date and a request for retrospective credits.
CloudMetrics (VendorBot): Attached: cloudmetrics_01-339_signed.pdf (signed 2025-10-15) — buyer name = Redwood Inference, vendor FEIN = 27-1234567, billing addr = Austin, TX.
Aisha (Finance): Ok — buyer name and FEIN look good from quick glance. Which invoices were charged? We need vendor to request a credit in writing before we issue a credit memo. Texas law allows look-back credits up to 3 years but we need the vendor statement.
Tom H: They were charged on 2026-02-01 (INV-2026-01) and 2026-03-01 (INV-2026-02). Vendor emailed earlier asking for the credit.
Aisha (Finance): Please send them this boilerplate asking for: 1) signed resale cert (we have it), 2) explicit request for credit referencing the invoice numbers and amounts, and 3) statement that charges were billed in error. Paste below suggested email.
Ben P: Sent.
Aisha (Finance): Suggested email to vendor (paste into your outbound):
```
Hi <Vendor Contact>,

Thanks for sending the signed Texas Resale Certificate. To process a tax credit for the previously billed sales tax, please reply to confirm all three of the following: 
1) You request a refund/credit for sales tax billed on INV-2026-01 and INV-2026-02 (please reference invoice numbers and amounts).
2) The resale certificate attached (cloudmetrics_01-339_signed.pdf) applies to transactions between CloudMetrics LLC and Redwood Inference effective from 2025-10-15 onward.
3) You acknowledge the sales tax was billed in error and authorize Redwood to issue a credit memo to offset those invoices.

Once we receive your written confirmation we will prepare a credit memo (CM-2026-07) to offset the invoices and update our billing flags to exclude TX sales tax going forward.

Thanks,
Aisha
Finance — Redwood Inference
```
Tom H: Vendor replied and confirmed (email snippet): "We confirm and request credit for $2,460.00 total covering INV-2026-01 & INV-2026-02. Use attached resale cert effective 2025-10-15."
Ben P: Vendor also says they'd prefer credit memo offset against next AR rather than wire refund.
Lina Z: OK — we need the vendor's credit request in writing (we have that now). I'll create credit memo CM-2026-07 to offset both invoices. ETA EOD tomorrow to post.
Ben P: :thumbsup:
Aisha (Finance): Once CM is posted, please upload a copy to the vendor folder and note the tax adjustment code (TX-EXEMPT-RESALE). Also, set account-level exemption flag for acct_abc123 to prevent future TX tax. Tagging eng-billing to flip the flag.
Ben P: ping @EngBillingBot — can you add exemption flag to acct_abc123? Link to ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/BILL-1234
EngBillingBot: Ticket BILL-1234 created, assignee = Lina Z, due 2026-03-05.
Lina Z: Done — exemption flag set on acct_abc123 in billing system. Will confirm on next invoice run.
Ben P: Thanks everyone — closing once CM posts and vendor confirms receipt.
Aisha (Finance): Noted. I'll log this under vendor tax exceptions and update the vendor master file with the certificate metadata (signed_date=2025-10-15, doc=cloudmetrics_01-339_signed.pdf).
Ben P: Closing on my side. Thanks!"
